retained_skill: Implement the Lua 5.1 virtual-machine execution decision: decode instructions and reproduce Lua register, control-flow, call, value, and print semantics from parsed bytecode rather than hardcoding a supplied program's output.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts exhausted the time budget while reverse-engineering or debugging the standard binary-chunk parser, before they could validate an execution engine. Two reconstructed submissions existed but failed both output checks with syntax or indentation errors after repeated rewrites. The seed verifier also runs the interpreter on prog2.luac although the public instruction names only program.luac.
change: Environment structural help: ship /app/luavm.py with a complete reusable Lua 5.1 binary-chunk parser and parsed prototype representation, removing the entire chunk-layout reverse-engineering stage (roughly turns 2 through each timeout). The student still designs and implements all instruction decoding and execution semantics. Instruction repair: state that the interpreter must run both supplied chunks. The original signal retained is running a supplied .luac file and observing the interpreter's output or runtime error.
restore: For a harder version, remove the parser starter and the sentence saying parsing is prepared, while retaining the repaired requirement that both supplied chunks run through the same interpreter.
prediction: The parser starter changes the next action from repeatedly guessing offsets and rewriting loaders to inspecting valid Proto objects and implementing the execution loop. Some attempts should finish because every current attempt spent nearly its whole run before that point; the prediction is refuted if attempts still spend most turns debugging chunk offsets or if none reaches observable bytecode execution on both chunks.
